final_answer: Lowering corporate tax rates may not boost long-term job growth because businesses might reinvest savings into stock buybacks or dividends rather than expanding operations. Additionally, tax cuts could reduce government revenue, limiting public investments in infrastructure or education that drive labor demand. If firms don’t face financial pressure to raise wages, they may not hire more workers. Moreover, tax cuts often benefit large corporations already dominating markets, rather than fostering new entrants that create jobs. Global competition could also dilute benefits, as other countries might match tax cuts, preventing sustained growth. Thus, tax cuts alone may not translate to meaningful job creation without配套 policies to direct investment toward labor-intensive sectors.
